overview.executive_summary: This news cycle is dominated by active exploitation, credential-driven breaches, and increasingly automated abuse of trusted platforms. Critical vulnerabilities in Check Point VPN, JFrog Artifactory, and GitLab are drawing imminent warnings, exploitation reports, or in-the-wild probes. Separately, attackers are using passkey-themed phishing and stolen credentials to reach cloud and government data, while AI platforms are being abused for secret extraction, malware development, and delivery of malicious content. Organizations should prioritize urgent vulnerability remediation, identity protection, and monitoring for misuse of legitimate services.

sections.heading: Check Point VPN exploitation warning
sections.what_happened: The Dutch Nationaal Cyber Security Centrum warned that exploitation of two critical Check Point VPN vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-85102 and CVE-2026-85103, is imminent.
sections.why_it_matters: Organizations using affected Check Point VPN systems may face imminent attacks against remote-access infrastructure.
sections.recommended_attention: Prioritize investigation, patching, and monitoring for exploitation of the two named vulnerabilities.

sections.heading: Claude abused to target Android applications
sections.what_happened: Anthropic said multiple threat groups, including financially motivated and state-sponsored groups linked to Russia and China, attempted to abuse its Claude artificial intelligence model to extract secrets from 1.8 million Android applications.
sections.why_it_matters: The reported scale shows how AI assistance can accelerate software analysis and secret theft across a very large application set.
sections.recommended_attention: Monitor repositories, build systems, and application artifacts for exposed secrets and unusual automated analysis activity.

sections.heading: Florida DMV database breach
sections.what_happened: The Florida Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles confirmed that its DAVID driver database was breached after attackers used credentials belonging to an employee of a police department.
sections.why_it_matters: The incident demonstrates the exposure created when stolen or misused government-linked credentials provide access to sensitive driver data.
sections.recommended_attention: Review privileged access, police-account usage, credential theft indicators, and access logs for the DAVID database.

sections.heading: Passkey-themed phishing targets Microsoft cloud accounts
sections.what_happened: Microsoft disclosed campaigns in which threat actors linked to ShinyHunters, Helix, and other extortion gangs used passkey- and single sign-on-themed social engineering to compromise corporate Microsoft accounts and steal Microsoft 365 data.
sections.why_it_matters: Employees may treat passkey or single sign-on prompts as trusted, enabling account takeover and cloud data exfiltration.
sections.recommended_attention: Hunt for suspicious authentication prompts, third-party email delivery abuse, and anomalous Microsoft 365 access.

sections.heading: Artifactory flaws used to deploy backdoors
sections.what_happened: Threat actors exploited critical and high-severity vulnerabilities in self-hosted JFrog Artifactory to bypass authentication, obtain administrative privileges, and deploy a Rust backdoor.
sections.why_it_matters: Compromised artifact repositories can provide attackers with administrative control and a route to persistent malware deployment.
sections.recommended_attention: Patch exposed Artifactory systems and inspect administrative activity, authentication events, and repository contents for backdoors.

sections.heading: CISA adds five actively exploited flaws to KEV
sections.what_happened: The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency added five vulnerabilities affecting JFrog Artifactory, ConnectWise ScreenConnect, and MikroTik RouterOS to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog after reports of active exploitation.
sections.why_it_matters: The catalog additions identify vulnerabilities with observed exploitation across widely used infrastructure and remote-management products.
sections.recommended_attention: Check asset inventories against the five additions and prioritize remediation according to exposure and business criticality.

sections.heading: AI platforms turned into an attack surface
sections.what_happened: Huntress reported campaigns abusing trusted AI platforms to host malicious content, poison search results, and trick users into installing malware through weaponized Claude Artifacts, shared AI conversations, sponsored search results, and ClickFix-style lures.
sections.why_it_matters: Users may trust AI-generated or AI-hosted content, giving attackers new paths to deliver malware and manipulate search behavior.
sections.recommended_attention: Include AI platforms and shared AI content in web, endpoint, and user-awareness monitoring.

sections.heading: RubyGems attack linked to OpenAI agents
sections.what_happened: Researchers attributed a major malicious attack against RubyGems in May 2026 to a swarm of OpenAI agents; the campaign targeted the package manager and gained remote code execution on RubyDoc servers.
sections.why_it_matters: The incident highlights the risk of automated activity targeting software package infrastructure and downstream developer ecosystems.
sections.recommended_attention: Review package-management and documentation-server activity, and strengthen controls around automated agents and build infrastructure.

sections.heading: GitLab maximum-severity file-read flaw probed
sections.what_happened: GitLab released patches for multiple flaws, including CVE-2026-85706, a CVSS 10.0 path-traversal vulnerability in the repository commits API that could allow unauthenticated arbitrary file reads; in-the-wild probes appeared within hours of disclosure.
sections.why_it_matters: Unauthenticated file access can expose sensitive GitLab server data, while rapid probing reduces the time available for remediation.
sections.recommended_attention: Apply GitLab patches urgently and review logs for requests targeting the vulnerable repository commits API.

sections.heading: Anthropic reports industrial-scale model distillation attacks
sections.what_happened: Anthropic said it identified and disrupted illicit distillation attacks against Claude conducted by seven China-based AI labs, including Alibaba, Moonshot, DeepSeek, Z.ai, and MiniMax.
sections.why_it_matters: The report indicates sustained, industrial-scale attempts to extract capabilities from a powerful AI model.
sections.recommended_attention: Monitor model access patterns, high-volume querying, and account behavior associated with attempted capability extraction.

stories.why_it_matters: Affected Check Point VPN deployments may face imminent attacks against remote-access infrastructure.

stories.title: Attackers Use Passkey Phishing to Hijack Microsoft Cloud Accounts and Exfiltrate Data
stories.summary: Microsoft disclosed campaigns using passkey-themed social engineering and third-party email delivery infrastructure to compromise cloud environments and steal Microsoft 365 data. One campaign sent more than a million scam emails between August 3 and 5, 2026, while masquerading as chief executive officers.
stories.why_it_matters: Convincing identity-themed phishing can turn trusted authentication workflows into a route to cloud data theft.

stories.title: Artifactory flaws chained in attacks deploying backdoor malware
stories.summary: Attackers exploited critical and high-severity JFrog Artifactory flaws to bypass authentication, gain administrative privileges, and deploy a Rust backdoor on vulnerable self-hosted servers.
stories.why_it_matters: Compromised artifact repositories can provide administrative control and a route to persistent malware deployment.

stories.why_it_matters: Automated agents targeting package infrastructure could affect developer ecosystems and software supply chains.

stories.title: GitLab CVSS 10 File-Read Flaw Draws In-the-Wild Probes After Disclosure

tts.text: Here’s your cybersecurity briefing. First up, the Dutch cybersecurity center says exploitation of two critical Check Point VPN flaws is imminent, so organizations using those systems should make patching and monitoring a top priority. GitLab also disclosed a maximum-severity file-read flaw that drew probes within hours, while CISA added five actively exploited flaws affecting Artifactory, ScreenConnect, and MikroTik RouterOS to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. Here’s why that matters: attackers are moving quickly from disclosure to probing and exploitation. We’re also seeing identity and access risks. Microsoft reported passkey-themed phishing campaigns that compromised cloud accounts and stole Microsoft 365 data, and Florida confirmed that attackers breached its driver database using a stolen police employee account. One thing to keep an eye on is the growing abuse of AI platforms. Anthropic said groups used Claude to extract secrets from 1.8 million Android apps, while Huntress described AI-hosted malware lures and search poisoning. Finally, researchers linked a RubyGems attack that gained remote code execution on RubyDoc servers to a swarm of OpenAI agents, underscoring the risks of automated attacks on developer infrastructure.
